svg.title: A client at 34 weeks reports a headache that has not eased with acetaminophen and "spots" in her vision. Blood pressure 172/112 , repeated at 168/110 fifteen minutes later. Reflexes 4+ with ankle clonus. Urine protein 3+. Platelets 88,000/mm 3 . Normal: urine protein negative to trace; platelets 150,000 to 400,000/mm³
svg.desc: Severe-range pressures on two readings with headache, visual change, hyperreflexia with clonus, proteinuria and a low platelet count define preeclampsia with severe features. Magnesium sulfate is given for seizure prophylaxis, and the environment is kept quiet with seizure precautions in place. Magnesium toxicity is tracked by reflexes, respiratory rate and urine output, because the drug is renally cleared and loss of reflexes is the earliest warning.

g.text: A client at 34 weeks reports a headache
that has not eased with acetaminophen and
a low platelet count define preeclampsia
